messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — during the backup-agent review I noticed the uploader serviceaccount keys look like they were minted with very low entropy on one staging cluster. Can we do a quick sanity check before we push to prod?
ajay.k: yikes. do you have the proof or just a hunch?
maria.g: found an entry in the agent logs showing a repeated nonce pattern in the CMK grant handshake. pasted snippet: ```2026-02-12T03:12:01Z uploader: grant_request nonce=0000...0000 grant_id=abc123```
kelly: that looks suspicious. could be a logging mask or maybe a bug in our randomness source in the init container. which uploader image tag?
maria.g: `uploader:v2.7.3` on staging-eu. also saw a similar but not identical pattern on staging-us with `v2.8.0-rc`.
encops-bot: @maria.g created incident INC-2026-042: low-entropy-kms-handshake-detected (sev:medium). Please triage.
sam.r: tagging ops-oncall — this touches snapshot encryption. if an attacker could predict nonce that's bad for replay protection.
ops-oncall: acknowledged. spinning up a canary to repro. can you attach the uploader pod log lines + the exact KMS provider (aws/kms vs hsm)?
maria.g: attached. provider is AWS KMS (cmk arn: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:123456789:key/xxxxx). logs attached inline; will DM more.
ajay.k: immediate mitigations: (1) rotate uploader service account creds, (2) deploy uploader image with explicit `/dev/urandom` usage and link against libcrypto patched in last PR, (3) add a KMS grant TTL <= 5m for uploads to reduce window.
kelly: agree. also enable and forward KMS Audit logs to our secure SIEM index (index:kms-audit-high) for the affected timeframe. we currently keep CloudTrail for 90d but need more accessible events for restores.
sam.r: curious — how are we currently doing grants? ephemeral STS + KMS grants or long-lived IAM role?
maria.g: uploader pods use a long-lived kube secret mounted into the agent for older clusters. new clusters use IRSA + short sts tokens. the long-lived secret is the risky part.
ops-oncall: can we rotate that secret and force IRSA on reprovision? what's the plan for on-prem/private where IRSA isn't available?
ajay.k: on-prem we should drop to HSM-backed KMS with a gateway and use mutual-TLS client certs rotated via our fleet CA. but that's bigger work. short term: limit IAM permissions & enforce per-bucket CMKs.
kelly: RBAC checklist: - blacklist old uploader secret in our PKI/secret-scan index - add admission webhook to block pods mounting `uploader-secret-old` - require `kms:Encrypt` be scoped to a single key alias for uploader role - add audit annotation to pod creation so we can trace who created it
sam.r: on the audit logging side, please ensure the KMS key policy includes a CloudTrail test principal, and add a log-based metric for `Decrypt` errors spikes — will help detect failed brute attempts.
maria.g: quick Q on permissions: if we move to ephemeral grants, do we still need the CMK in IAM policy or is KMS grant+sts enough?
ajay.k: good question. for AWS KMS best practice: use least-privileged IAM to call `GenerateDataKey*` only via a short-lived role, and issue KMS grants scoped to that role. that avoids needing long-lived IAM creds with KMS policy on them.
ops-oncall: repro attempt shows the uploader binary was reading from `/dev/random` but with `O_NONBLOCK` incorrectly set in the init script. I'm patching to force `getrandom()` syscall.
kelly: after patch, let's run: ```kubectl apply -f uploader-patch.yaml && ./stress-test-backup --runs 50 --check-nonce```. Also add a unit-test that validates no repeated nonces in 100k iterations.
sam.r: for recovery/incident response: 1) rotate CMK grants and rotate any long-lived secrets, 2) re-encrypt last 24h of snapshots with fresh data keys, 3) block restore operations until audit confirms no key compromise, 4) notify customers if any tenant-specific keys were affected.
ajay.k: addendum — for re-encrypt we should use a rolling job that rewraps object-store blobs with a new envelope key, not re-download everything. we have safe server-side rewrap tooling for S3/GS.
maria.g: will prepare a runbook and PR for the webhook + secret rotation. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
encops-bot: INC-2026-042 status updated -> triage-in-progress. assigned: maria.g, ajay.k
kelly: leaving a note: postmortem action items should include a KMS integration test in our CI that validates nonce entropy and grant lifecycle. low-cost catch.
ops-oncall: closing loop — patched uploader image built as `uploader:v2.7.4-hotfix`, pushed to staging, secret rotated, cloudtrail forwarding enabled. will monitor logs and escalate if we see anomalies. :eyes:
